what_was_remembered: *** HIS SURNAME WAS MARINO. *** "Mary Septima Taylor is said to have gone out to South Africa to work for a widower by the name of ROBERT (or ROBERTO) MARINO who lived in the Cape Town area."
source: Sue Rowbotham, Three Corners of the Land, section "Mary Septima Taylor"
grade: *** THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN EITHER SOURCE ***
what_this_archive_can_say: The Devon family, who knew him only through what Mary Septima told them, remembered his surname as *** MARINO *** - not Lerena, and not anything close to it phonetically. *** Marino is one of the commonest surnames in Italy. *** This archive has argued, from two companies' independent ethnicity readings, that Pablo Armando carried Italian ancestry. Here, from a wholly separate direction and written down before any DNA was tested, an English family says he was called Marino. *** IT PROVES NOTHING AND IT IS THE BEST CORROBORATION THE ITALIAN READING HAS. *** It could equally be his mother's surname, a name he used, or a Devon mishearing across a hundred years.

what_was_remembered: "Roberto had three sons; Louis, Cardo and Nuno. It is not clear whether any of the children were Mary's."
grade: memory, and demonstrably wrong in part
what_this_archive_can_say: Louis = Roque Luis Armando, Cardo = Ricardo Juan Carlos, Nuno = Nuno Fernando. *** The three sons are right. The widower-with-children is wrong: *** Roque's baptism at Corpus Christi Wynberg names Mary Septima as his MOTHER, and the 1911 marriage register calls Pablo Armando a BACHELOR and Mary Septima a SPINSTER. He was no widower and they were not his by another woman.

what_was_remembered: "I heard they met on a ship, fell in love, built a life in the Cape with their three children."
what_this_archive_can_say: Untested. No passenger list for either of them has been found, by David, by Cheryl or by this archive. *** It is the oldest surviving account of how they met and it is worth one search of the right manifests. ***

what_was_remembered: *** THEY ARE BURIED AT NEWLANDS CEMETERY, CAPE TOWN, IN AN UNMARKED GRAVE THAT CARRIES ONLY THE WORD "LERENA". ***
source: Cheryl to Sue, 30 June 2020, from her sister Patricia's visit to the site office
what_this_archive_can_say: Newlands is where he died - No. 7 Forth Road. A photograph of the grave was attached to that email. *** This archive has never recorded a burial place for either of them. ***

what_was_remembered: *** THERE IS A THIRD PERSON IN THAT GRAVE: A BABY GIRL, CAREEN MARIA LERENA, BORN AND DIED 1947. ***
source: Cheryl to Sue, 30 June 2020, from the cemetery office
what_this_archive_can_say: *** This archive has never heard of her. *** 1947 - Pablo Armando was sixty-five and had been a widower twelve years. Cheryl's own reading is that Rose Lilian Theys was the mother. That is an inference by a granddaughter, not a record, and it is recorded here as hers. A Cape birth and death registration of 1947 would settle it.

what_was_remembered: "My Grandfather got involved with a woman by the name of Rose Theys... I think they did marry, however we do not know anything about her. When my Grandfather died she took everything."
grade: memory, and the documents contradict half of it
what_this_archive_can_say: *** THEY DID NOT MARRY. *** His death notice of 28 March 1950 says "Widower", names no surviving spouse, and gives his pre-deceased spouse as Mary Septima. The 1950 liquidation account describes Rose Lilian Theys as a SPINSTER and "no relation" - and she signed the death notice herself, as *** Executrix Nominate, present at death. *** On "she took everything" the account is closer to the family's memory than to the archive's: the three sons shared one quarter between them and she took the rest.

what_was_remembered: *** A NEWSPAPER REPORT: Roberto was fined five pounds for shooting at two native boys who were trying to steal - a horse? - from him. A cutting was, or is, held by the Taylor/Braddick family in north Devon. ***
what_this_archive_can_say: Neither Sue nor Cheryl could place it. *** A fine of five pounds means a magistrate's court and a date, and Cape newspapers of the period are digitised. *** It would be the earliest independent description of him in South Africa outside a register.

what_was_remembered: The horses did not stop. Cousin Carlos was a jockey and became Chairman of the South African Jockey Association; his son Gavin is a jockey; Carlos's sister Theresa's son Brandon is a jockey who moved to Australia; cousin "Spike" is a trainer and breeder with his own stables.
grade: living people - named and nothing more
what_this_archive_can_say: *** Four generations of the turf, from a horse-dealer at Diep River in 1911. *** Living people are named here only because Cheryl named them to a cousin in a letter, and nothing further about them is recorded.

what_was_remembered: "Uncle Louis married Uncle Cardo's wife's mother, hence obviously the reason they were closer. So they were mother and daughter and also sisters-in-law."
what_this_archive_can_say: *** This is exactly the relationship this archive derived from the AutoClusters on 16 September 2026, hours before the letter was read. *** Roseline/Rosina Wilhelmina (m.1 Chappell, m.2 Lerena) married Roque; her daughter by Chappell, Doreen May, married Ricardo. Memory and chromosome agree, and neither knew of the other.

what_was_remembered: Pam and Juanita, daughters of Uncle Louis, were ballet dancers who left South Africa young for London.
what_this_archive_can_say: Roque's 1973 death notice names his two surviving children as *** JUANITA RAMOND HUTSON (born LERENA) *** and *** PANOLA MARIA LERENA. *** "Panola" is Pam.

what_was_remembered: Mary Septima was born at Northam, Devon, on 17 September 1884, the seventh daughter; a pupil-teacher, "school mistress", aged 16 at the census of April 1901.
grade: *** CONFIRMED - and it settles a discrepancy ***
what_this_archive_can_say: The 1911 marriage register gives her age as 27, which would need a birth in 1883. *** Sue's date, her Northam baptism and the GRO registration all say 1884, so the register is wrong by a year and the archive keeps 17 September 1884. ***

what_was_remembered: *** Both her parents were dead before she left: her mother Mary Ann Hellen Taylor, born Brayley, died in 1900; her father William Taylor died in November 1902. Sue finds NO SIGN OF HER IN ENGLAND AFTER THE 1901 CENSUS. ***
what_this_archive_can_say: *** She was orphaned at eighteen and gone by nineteen. *** The window for her emigration is 1901 to late 1905, and Roque was born at Cape Town in November 1905. That is the tightest bracket this archive has ever had on her arrival.

what_was_remembered: *** HER BROTHER WAS IN THE CAPE BEFORE HER. *** Horace Archibald "Archie" Taylor was posted to South Africa on 21 October 1899 and served in the Second Boer War until 15 September 1902, winning the Queen's South Africa Medal with Cape Colony clasp and the King's South Africa Medal.
source: Sue Rowbotham, from regimental and army pension records
what_this_archive_can_say: *** A nineteen-year-old orphan does not sail to the Cape at random. *** Her brother had spent three years there and came home the year her father died. This archive had no explanation at all for why she went; now it has a plausible one, and a named man to look for in Cape records.

what_was_remembered: She returned to England in the summer of 1935, stayed about three months with her sister Edie Dalling at 26 Fore Street, Northam, and brought crates of grapes. She had cancer; the family knew they would not see her again; there was a large family gathering and many photographs. She died shortly after she got home.
what_this_archive_can_say: She died 15 November 1935. *** So the last voyage was made knowing it was the last, and there are photographs of it in Devon. *** The archive holds one image captioned "Mary Septima Burial" and has not looked for the 1935 gathering photographs at all.

what_was_remembered: Nuno Fernando died of a coronary thrombosis at forty-six. Cheryl was fifteen. "My Father never discussed his parents with me or my siblings so we never knew anything about either of them."
what_this_archive_can_say: *** This is why the archive exists, and it is also why the 1971 death notice names no parents. *** His widow wrote "Deceased" against father and mother because there was nothing in the house to write.
